title: No AI Slop: A Manifesto
lede: Speakers and attendees of AIE Code Summit 2026 wrote a manifesto, modelled on the Agile Manifesto, that defines AI slop and sets out how teams should own the quality of AI-assisted work.

points: Five values put outcomes ahead of output, understanding ahead of speed, and fixing the system ahead of patching output.
Slop is defined as work that took less effort to make than it demands from the person reading it.
It calls slop asymmetric: generating a huge PR or long doc is nearly free, while reviewing it costs as much as ever.
Signers commit to flagging agent-written content, checking what matters before sending, and politely returning slop they receive.
Repeat mistakes should become guardrails, with linters, type checkers and automated checks catching whatever they can.

points.text: Readers single out the line that what shipped and who it helps matters far more than lines of code, PRs or tokens spent.
Reviewing huge AI-generated PRs is a recurring worry; one suggests attaching the prompt, and a reply notes real pipelines involve far more than one prompt.
One commenter argues slop is a human failing, the old shovelware problem; a reply counters that LLMs make it vastly cheaper to produce.
Some question the framing, asking whether matching everyone else's output is really bad and whether a negative name serves the cause.
